title: Edge and CDN — concept map
intro: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) caches responses at edge locations near users so round-trip time drops and your origin serves fewer requests. Amazon CloudFront is AWS's CDN: you define a distribution with origins (S3, API Gateway, ALB, custom HTTP), cache behaviors that route paths to origins, and TTL policies that control freshness. This module covers why CDNs matter, how distributions work, cache keys and invalidation, locking down S3 with Origin Access Control (OAC), and fronting APIs for global latency and DDoS absorption.

conceptCards.title: Why a CDN
conceptCards.summary: Edge caches cut latency, absorb traffic spikes, and shield origins. Cache only what is safe to repeat.
conceptCards.example: React bundle served from Mumbai edge instead of us-east-1 S3

conceptCards.title: Distributions
conceptCards.summary: One distribution = domain + origins + ordered cache behaviors. Default behavior catches unmatched paths.

conceptCards.title: Cache keys & TTL
conceptCards.summary: Key = path + query + selected headers/cookies. TTL from Cache-Control or min/default/max. Invalidate costs money.
conceptCards.example: Cache key ignores Authorization → one cached response for all users (bad)

conceptCards.title: S3 + OAC
conceptCards.summary: Block public S3. CloudFront signs requests with OAC. Legacy OAI is deprecated for new setups.
conceptCards.example: Bucket policy allows s3:GetObject only from your distribution ARN

conceptCards.title: API / ALB origins
conceptCards.summary: Forward dynamic paths to API Gateway or ALB. Disable caching or use short TTL. Preserve Host and auth headers.
